newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary bourse merger possible but not imminent.
newsitem.headline: Hungary bourse merger possible but not imminent.

text.p: Hungary's new securities law would make a merger of the Stock Exchange (BSE) and the Commodity Exchange (BCE) possible but cooperation talks are still in a preliminary phase, BCE officials said on Wednesday.

"The BCE general meeting has approved a proposal that the bourse (BCE) council should start exploring cooperation possibilities between the two bourses," BCE President and CEO Andrea Varga Pongracz told Reuters following the BCE general meeting.
"This cooperation could both mean a merger or a division of the markets," she said.
However, the BCE meeting did not vote on the merger itself.
BCE board chairman Szergej Keresztesi said earlier that the BSE had broached the merger idea in August and the BCE was just reacting to their proposal.
The BCE has total daily turnover of about 3.0 to 4.0 billion forints ($18.86- $25.14 million) and the 1996 total was expected to be between 800 and 900 billion forints.
The BSE had daily spot share turnover of around one billion forints.
